children: The partnership targets material localisation and supply chain development around the Dholera fabrication project

Tata Electronics has partnered with Fujifilm Corporation to support the development of India’s semiconductor materials ecosystem and strengthen supplies for the upcoming semiconductor fabrication facility in Dholera, Gujarat. The collaboration will focus on advanced materials, local manufacturing capabilities and supply chain development for semiconductor production.

The partnership will involve the development and supply of materials required for semiconductor manufacturing. Tata Electronics and Fujifilm will work towards building a more localised supply chain around the Dholera facility, with the aim of supporting material availability closer to manufacturing operations.

The collaboration comes as India seeks to develop capabilities across different stages of the semiconductor value chain, including chip fabrication and the production of materials and chemicals required by semiconductor facilities.

A key part of the partnership will be the localisation of critical raw materials used in semiconductor manufacturing. The companies will also work with Indian chemical manufacturers to support the development of domestic production capabilities.

Fujifilm will provide technology, quality assurance and manufacturing expertise as part of the collaboration. The support is expected to help Indian suppliers address the technical and quality requirements associated with semiconductor materials.

Fujifilm is also planning to establish a semiconductor materials manufacturing facility in Dholera, Gujarat. The proposed facility will add to the materials infrastructure developing around India’s semiconductor manufacturing plans.

The move could create closer links between materials production and semiconductor fabrication in the region, while providing domestic manufacturers with an opportunity to participate in the emerging supply chain.

For Tata Electronics, access to locally developed materials will be relevant as semiconductor manufacturing capacity develops at Dholera. For Fujifilm, the planned manufacturing presence provides a base to supply materials to India’s expanding semiconductor industry.

The partnership reflects the growing focus on developing domestic capabilities beyond semiconductor fabrication itself. Materials, speciality chemicals and manufacturing inputs form an important part of the wider semiconductor supply chain.

By combining materials expertise with local manufacturing capabilities, the collaboration is aimed at increasing domestic participation in this part of the semiconductor ecosystem. The companies will also work on technology and quality processes needed to support Indian chemical manufacturers.
The development of local suppliers could gradually reduce dependence on overseas sources for selected semiconductor materials while creating additional manufacturing capabilities around the sector.
